title: Policy synthesizer for conservative batching/caching suggestions with progressive quality gates
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Build a policy synthesizer that generates conservative batching and KV-cache configuration recommendations, and attaches progressive quality gates (evaluation checks + thresholds) that run automatically during canary/rollout and trigger safe rollback or staged traffic increases.

Why: Cost advisor suggestions are valuable but risky — overly aggressive batching or cache TTLs can regress output quality for downstream features. Rather than a binary allow/block, we need a reproducible, auditable policy that: 1) synthesizes conservative starting configs from workload signals, 2) defines an evaluation plan (sample size, metrics, thresholds), and 3) wires automatic enforcement (block/roll back/notify) during apply. This reduces operator overhead and prevents silent regressions.

Scope:
- Inputs: recent request distribution (seq len histogram, prefix reuse rate), model variant capabilities, deployment tier (hosted/dedicated), and historical eval baselines for a customer's golden prompts if available.
- Output: a set of recommended config deltas (batch size, latency SLO target, KV-cache TTL/profile), a progressive rollout plan (shadow -> canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%), and an eval plan containing: sample harness, metrics, acceptance thresholds, and statistical test to run at each stage.
- Enforcement: integrate with rollout controller to gate stage progression. On failure, auto-rollback to previous stable config and create an incident with diagnostics.

Key components and decisions:
1) Synthesizer algorithm: rule-based prioritization + heuristic scaling. Start with conservative multiplier (e.g., suggested_batch = max(1, floor(current_batch * 0.75))) and use sequence-length buckets to recommend per-route batching windows. Attach confidence band based on sample size and model latency variance.

2) Evaluation harness: reuse existing golden-prompt harness but add a statistical assertion layer. Each gate must specify: metric (semantic similarity w/ embeddings; exact-structure match for tool outputs; hallucination score; generation entropy), baseline measurement window, min sample size, and p-value threshold. Default: paired bootstrap with 10k resamples and alpha 0.05, with minimum N=200 per variant for high-confidence routes.

3) Acceptance thresholds: configurable per-customer and per-route, with safe defaults: semantic similarity drop < 1.5% absolute OR no regression in structured-field exact-match > 0.5%. For high-risk routes (billing, legal copy, auth flows) require zero regression tolerance and additional manual approval.

4) Monitoring & observability: emit per-gate events to Console (gate.start, gate.finish, gate.fail) with cost delta estimates, sample summary, and links to evaluation artifacts. Add prebuilt dashboard tile showing candidate config, projected monthly savings, and quality delta.

5) Rollout policy integration: progressive schedule plus backoff. Example: shadow(24h) -> canary(5%, 1h) -> canary(25%, 2h) -> 100%. If gate fail at any stage, immediate rollback and mark the suggestion as "unsafe" for 7 days.

6) Human-in-the-loop: support an "auto-apply: on/off" flag. Default OFF for enterprise customers until 2 successful auto-applies across different models. Provide audit log entry with author, timestamp, and attached eval report per apply.

Artifacts/links: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.internal/redwood/auto-cost-policy-synthesizer (DRAFT); GitHub RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/267; Draft dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/d/optimize/policy-synthesizer

Success criteria:
- End-to-end pipeline can generate a recommendation and associated eval plan within 60s for a given route.
- At least one pilot customer completes a staged apply with no observed quality regression and achieves >=15% token cost reduction on the pilot route.
- Gate automation triggers rollback in synthetic failure cases 100% of the time during tests.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: too-small sample sizes cause false negatives. Mitigation: conservative defaults, min sample sizes, and require manual override for low-volume routes.
- Risk: metric mismatch (semantic sim not capturing downstream acceptability). Mitigation: allow route owners to plug in custom metrics and golden prompts.

Next steps (implementation roadmap):
1) Week 1-2: implement synthesizer engine + config schema, wire to Optimize recommendations API.
2) Week 3: implement evaluation harness integration, bootstrap default thresholds and statistical tests.
3) Week 4: integrate with rollout controller and Console events, add dashboard tiles.
4) Week 5-6: pilot with 2 internal routes, collect telemetry and adjust thresholds.

Longer-term: incorporate automated A/B population stratification, workload-aware sample allocation, and ML-based regressors to predict quality regression probability given a config delta.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Synthesizer produces recommendations and an eval plan for a demo route. 2) Evaluation harness runs the gate tests and reports pass/fail into Console. 3) Rollout controller enforces gate decisions and can auto-rollback. 4) Pilot shows >=15% token cost reduction on at least one route without failing gates.
